tier_reason: The measurements come from a peer-reviewed paper (Bassoy, ICCS 2019, Springer LNCS pp. 32-45) that compares TTV with Eigen, TCL and TBLIS; the README repeats its setup (i9-7900X, GCC 7.3, -Ofast -march=native -fopenmp, OpenBLAS 0.2.20) and its plots. Not A, because the harness that runs TCL/TBLIS/Eigen is not public: test/ holds only gtest unit tests, example/ holds interface demos and misc/ holds only PNG plots.

corrections.claimed_speedup: The README has no speedups in text, only plots. Approximate values read from the README PNG plots (misc/*_speedup_*.png), per test case: over Eigen (sequential), about 3x to 300x on symmetric tensors and up to about 900x on asymmetric single-precision tensors; over TBLIS, about 1x to 17x, mostly 2-8x; over TCL, about 0.3x to 35x, so TTV is slower than TCL in some cases. On symmetric single-precision tensors TTV reaches about 20-35 Gflop/s, against up to about 31 for TCL, about 15 for TBLIS and about 8 for Eigen. The paper's abstract, seen only as a search-engine snippet because the paper itself could not be opened, says TTV is on average 6.1x and up to 12.6x faster than TCL's TTGT implementation and reaches 34.8 Gflop/s in single precision.
corrections.caveats: The repo has no benchmark harness for the TCL/TBLIS/Eigen comparison (test/ holds gtest unit tests only, misc/ holds PNG plots only), so the README plots cannot be reproduced from the repo. Speedups appear only as scatter plots, so the per-case values are approximate readings. In several cases TTV is slower than TCL (plotted speedup below 1). Eigen ran sequentially while TTV ran in parallel on 10 cores/20 threads, which inflates the Eigen ratios; the 100-900x Eigen points are not like for like. TTV calls OpenBLAS/MKL gemv/dot and is not faster than BLAS itself, so this is really a tensor-contraction entry rather than a BLAS replacement. The experiments date from 2019 and use GCC 7.3, OpenBLAS 0.2.20, TCL 0.1.1, TBLIS 1.0.0 and Eigen 3.3.90. LICENSE.txt is LGPL-3.0, while the README badge just says GPL. The verifier could not open the ICCS paper (Springer, iccs-meeting.org and Fraunhofer hosts are blocked).

notes: The repo exists and is not a fork or archived; it has 24 stars, 5 forks, the LGPL-3.0 license (LICENSE.txt) and a last commit on 2025-11-02. The B tier rests on the paper's ICCS 2019 venue and its abstract numbers (6.1x average, 12.6x maximum over TCL), which were seen only through search-engine snippets. The orchestrator might move this entry from blas-lapack to a tensor-contraction category.
